scope: Eight bounded errexit contracts through four shell aliases compare native GNU and the immutable candidate: local function state, explicit subshell bodies, nested eval, EXIT/ERR traps, conditional suppression, inherited substitution errors and lastpipe failure. Exact output/status and all child Valgrind summaries are retained. These are ordinary shell control-flow inputs.

results.name: bash:function
args: -c
set -e; f(){ local x=inside; false; printf unreachable; }; f; printf unreachable

results.name: bash:function-subshell
args: -c
set -e; f() (false; printf unreachable); f; printf unreachable

results.name: bash:nested-eval
args: -c
set -e; f(){ local x=inside; g; }; g(){ eval "false; printf unreachable"; }; f

results.name: bash:exit-local
args: -c
set -e; trap 'printf "exit:%s:%s\n" "$?" "${x-unset}"' EXIT; f(){ local x=inside; false; }; f

results.name: bash:error-trap
args: -c
set -eE; trap 'printf "error:%s\n" "$?"' ERR; f(){ local x=inside; false; }; f

results.name: bash:conditional-ignore
args: -c
set -e; f(){ local x=inside; false; printf "continued:%s\n" "$x"; }; if f; then printf "outer:%s\n" "${x-unset}"; fi

results.name: bash:substitution
args: -c
set -e; shopt -s inherit_errexit; f(){ local x=inside; false; printf unreachable; }; value=$(f); printf unreachable

results.name: bash:lastpipe-failure
args: -c
set -e; shopt -s lastpipe; f(){ local x=inside; printf "item\n" | { read -r x; false; }; }; f
